'''''Genista stenopetala''''', the '''sweet broom''', '''Easter broom''' or '''leafy broom''' ([[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''Genista spachiana'', ''Cytisus spachianus''), is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the legume [[family (botany)|family]] Fabaceae, native to the [[Canary Islands]], on [[La Palma]] and [[Tenerife]].

== Etymology ==
The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''stenopetala'' means "with narrow petals".<ref name="RHSLG">{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |year=2012 |isbn=978-1845337315 |location=United Kingdom}}</ref>

== Description ==
It is an [[evergreen]] shrub growing to {{convert|3|m}} tall. The leaves are trifoliate, the leaflets {{convert|1|-|3|cm}} long, narrow elliptic, coated with fine silky, silvery hairs. The strongly scented flowers are yellow, {{convert|1|-|2|cm}} long, produced in [[raceme]]s {{convert|5|-|11|cm}} long. The flowers appear in late winter or early spring.<ref name = RHSPF/> The fruit is a [[legume|pod]] {{convert|2|-|3|cm}} long.

Under the name ''Genista'' × ''spachiana'', it has won the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/65679/Genista-x-spachiana/Details | title = ''Genista'' × ''spachiana'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 9 July 2020}}</ref> It is not a [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] plant, and does not tolerate temperatures below {{convert|5 |C|F|abbr=on}}, so in [[temperate climate|temperate]] climates it is usually grown under glass. However, it may be placed outside during the summer months, in a sheltered, sunny spot.<ref name = RHSPF/>
